texts.preamble: Abha Garg vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2017 Mcrc-12131-2011 (Abha Garg Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 06-02-2017 Shri Kunal Dubey, learned counsel for the petitioner. Shri A.R.S. Chouhan, learned Panel Lawyer for respondent No.1/State. This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed to invoke the extra ordinary jurisdiction of this Court and to quash the proceeding of Complaint Case No.10412/2008 pending before the Special Judge (under the Municipality Act), Jabalpur for offences punishable under Sections 7 and 16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Briefly stated the prosecution story is that respondent No.2/B.S. Jamod, the Food Inspector of Jabalpur filed a complaint case before the Court of Special Magistrate (under the Municipal Act) Jabalpur for offence under Sections 7 and 16 (1) (a) (i) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 read with Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules. It is contented that the Food Inspector taken a sample from one Baliram Pandey who was carrying milk in Autorickshaw bearing Registration No.M.P.-20-LA-1120. The driver/Baliram Pandey informed the inspector that the milk belongs to the petitioner. Three samples of the milk were seized and one sample was sent to State Food Laboratory, Bhopal for examination. Another sample was sent to the Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Bhopal while the third sample was deposited with the Local Heath Authority, Mandla. It is contented that the report of sample which was sent for analysis was received with report dated 04/06/2008. It is found that the sample of milk is adulterated. However, compliance of Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 was not made and no notice was given to the petitioner, therefore, the petitioner was deprived of his rights. The petitioner, therefore, claimed that as there is violation of the provisions envisaged, the complaint against the petitioner deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Counsel for the respondent/State opposed the contentions. Sub Section 2 of Section 13 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 provides that, when the report of the analysis shows that the article of food is adulterated and a prosecution has been instituted, Sub Section 2 requires its Local (Health) Authority to send a copy of the report to the accused and to intimate to him that he may make an application to the Court to get the second part of the sample analyzed by the Central Food Abha Garg vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9537447/ 1 Laboratory. Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance in the case of Ravindra Chopade Vs. State of M.P. reported as 2013(1) Mpwn 118, in which it is held that accused was deprived of valuable right to get the sample analyzed before expiry date of the product- proceedings [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Counsel for the petitioner also placed reliance on Prahlad Gattani & others Vs. State of M.P. reported as 2012(4) Mpht 358, in which it is held that, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, Sections 7/16 and 13- Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, Rule 32(b) (2) (v)- Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, Section 482- Delay in forwarding notice under Section 13(2) of the Act along with copy of report of Public Analyst-The sample of Ketch, drawn by the Food Inspector was forwarded for analysis to Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Bhopal-
